previous_versions: 1.0 (January 15, 1996) — first public version; LS 1.5 / FS 12 Mb/s.
1.1 (September 23, 1998) — added Interrupt-OUT, removed PMM mode, errata.
2.0 (April 27, 2000) — added High-speed 480 Mb/s; introduced Transaction Translator + Split Transactions for HS-hub-to-FS/LS-device bridging.

key_changes.summary: First production version; two speeds (LS 1.5 / FS 12 Mb/s); 4 transfer types; hub-based topology.
Added High-Speed 480 Mb/s + chirp handshake at attach + Transaction Translator + Split transactions + microframes (125 µs) + NYET handshake + PING flow control + HS test modes.

backward_compat_traps.USB_1_x_device: Does not chirp K at reset; stays at FS or LS.
backward_compat_traps.USB_2_0_HS_device: Chirps K to negotiate HS; falls back to FS if no chirp-J-K-J-K-J response.
backward_compat_traps.trap: HS device on USB 1.1 host will silently fall back to FS — bandwidth surprise for users.

backward_compat_traps.USB_1_x_hub: Forwards all transactions at FS/LS only.
backward_compat_traps.USB_2_0_hub: Has internal Transaction Translator (TT); HS upstream + FS/LS downstream; bridged via Start-Split + Complete-Split.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Plugging USB 2.0 HS device into a USB 1.1 hub forces FS — even if downstream of a USB 2.0 root hub. Insert a USB 2.0 hub to recover HS.

backward_compat_traps.HS_endpoint: May additionally respond NYET (accepted but not ready for next); host uses PING to re-check.
backward_compat_traps.trap: USB 1.1 hosts will not understand NYET; HS-capable devices respond NYET only when running at HS.
Forgetting to clear ENDPOINT_HALT after a STALL leaves the toggle frozen; subsequent transactions silently dropped.

fields.version_naming_history_note: USB-IF (USB Implementers Forum) maintains the spec. Original specifiers were Compaq, HP, Intel, Lucent, Microsoft, NEC, Philips (the 'Promoter Group'). Later revisions: USB 3.0 (2008) added SuperSpeed 5 Gb/s; USB 3.1 (2013) 10 Gb/s; USB 3.2 (2017) 20 Gb/s; USB4 (2019) 40 Gb/s.
